Morbegno
mor-bay'nyo
n. (town of the lower Valtellina; seat of a Reformed congregation destroyed in the massacre of 1620)
Italian Morbegno, of uncertain origin, perhaps from a Lombard personal name; the town stands in the lower Valtellina near the head of Lake Como.

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

Morbegno is the chief town of the lower Valtellina, at the end of the valley nearest Lake Como and the Milanese frontier, and under the Grisons administration it held one of the Reformed congregations of the valley. Its position made it the most exposed of them: it was the first place reached from Spanish Milan, its Catholic population was in constant contact with the archbishop's clergy across the border, and the Capuchin and Jesuit mission to the valley worked chiefly from this end of it. When the rising came in July 1620 the lower valley moved first, and the congregation at Morbegno was among those destroyed; the ministers who did not escape over the passes were killed with their people. After 1620 the valley was closed to Reformed worship, and the treaties which ended the Valtellina wars confirmed it; no Reformed congregation was restored there. The dictionary enters Morbegno as the companion of Sondrio and for one further point. A frontier congregation is not simply a congregation in a dangerous place. It is the place where a church finds out what it has actually taught, because a people under that kind of pressure either know why they believe what they believe or they do not, and nobody can tell them in the week it is tested.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines a mission as a body of persons sent to propagate religion; exposed as laid open, unprotected; and extirpation as the act of rooting out.

expand to see more

MISSION, n. [L. missio.] A sending or being sent; persons sent; a station of missionaries; the act of sending to propagate religion.

EXPOSED, adj. Laid open; made bare; put in danger; unprotected; not covered or defended.

EXTIRPATION, n. [L. extirpatio.] The act of rooting out; eradication; excision; total destruction.

FRONTIER, n. The border or confine of a country, bordering on another country; the marches.

TREATY, n. [Fr. traite.] An agreement, league or contract between two or more nations or sovereigns, formally signed.

Modern Corruption

Lower Valtellina town, the most exposed of the valley's Reformed congregations, destroyed in July 1620 and never restored.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The dictionary records what the Valtellina mission actually was on the Catholic side, without either exaggeration or excuse: a sustained, intelligent and well-funded effort by the Capuchins and the Jesuits, working from Milan across a political frontier, to recover a valley by preaching, schools and charity. It largely succeeded before the massacre, and the massacre completed by violence what the mission had begun by argument. Naming the first half honestly is part of naming the second half justly.

The principle to recover is that catechising is the defence of a frontier congregation. “Holding fast the faithful word as he hath been taught, that he may be able by sound doctrine both to exhort and to convince the gainsayers” (Tit 1:9) is written of a minister, and what is required of the minister has to be worked into the people. “Beloved, think it not strange concerning the fiery trial which is to try you” (1Pe 4:12) is the apostle's warning that the trial is normal; the church which has told its people so, and taught them why, has done what can be done.

Greek antilego (G483) — to speak against, to gainsay; “to convince the gainsayers”, Titus 1:9.

Greek thlipsis (G2347) — pressure, tribulation; “through much tribulation enter into the kingdom of God”, Acts 14:22.
